fix(release): sign the container image with cosign v3 and move it to dockers_v2

The 0.11.3 release failed while signing the Docker image ([run](https://github.com/compute-blade-community/compute-blade-agent/actions/runs/44520556509/job/135548122492)):

```
Error: must enable upload to the OCI registry or specify a local --bundle path with --new-bundle-format
```

`docker_signs` passed `--upload=false`. With cosign v2 that produced a signature that was thrown away. Cosign v3 (since #214) writes the new Sigstore bundle format by default and refuses to sign without either uploading or a local bundle path. This was the first release since that switch, so nobody had hit it yet.

Dropping the flag lets cosign attach the bundle to the image in ghcr.io. That's also the only place `cosign verify` looks, so the image signature becomes checkable for the first time:

```sh
cosign verify ghcr.io/compute-blade-community/compute-blade-agent:<tag> \
  --certificate-oidc-issuer=https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com \
  --certificate-identity=https://github.com/compute-blade-community/compute-blade-agent/.github/workflows/release.yaml@refs/heads/main
```

The workflow already logs in to ghcr.io and runs with `write-all`, so the push needs no further permissions.

## dockers_v2

While in here, the image moves from the deprecated `dockers` to `dockers_v2`, which builds and pushes the image in one `docker buildx build --push`. Two things change with it.

goreleaser now puts the binaries under `<os>/<arch>/` in the build context, so the Dockerfile copies them from there:

```dockerfile
ARG TARGETPLATFORM
COPY $TARGETPLATFORM/compute-blade-agent $TARGETPLATFORM/bladectl /bin/
```

`docker_signs` drops `artifacts: all` (the default now picks the `dockers_v2` images) and signs `${artifact}@${digest}`, so the signature covers the pushed digest instead of whatever a tag points to at signing time.

The published image becomes an index with an SBOM attestation attached, since `dockers_v2` turns `sbom` on by default. It's still arm64 only, under the same three tags.

I checked it with `mise run snapshot` locally: the image builds, both binaries are in `/bin` and run, and the OCI labels are set. The `snapshot` CI job on this PR builds it again. Signing and pushing only happen in the real release.

## Recovering 0.11.3

The v0.11.3 release exists but has no assets, and the `v0.11.3`, `v0` and `latest` images were pushed unsigned. Re-running the failed job would check out the same commit with the old config, so merging this as a `fix` lets release-please cut 0.11.4 with everything published and signed. The empty v0.11.3 release can be deleted afterwards.

fix(client): a collapsed particle frame no longer stops the renderer

## Summary

- `inverseInto` (particle-graph.ts) threw `Singular particle motion matrix` on a zero determinant. Nothing on the emitter path (`characters.ts advanceEmitter` -> `advanceGraphEmitter` -> `advanceParticleGraph`) catches it. So `renderer.ts frameFailed` set its sticky failure, and the renderer drew nothing for the rest of the session.
- A zero rotation axis produces exactly that frame: `particle-rotation.ts` turns it into a zero basis, and `dun/bagh_masin_bridge01_l.efp` authors one. A kept-matrix element then inverts its previous frame on every tick (`keptDelta`).
- The port now follows the original: a zero determinant inverts to the frame itself, so the element multiplies by its own frame. The `1e-12` epsilon goes too, because the native only tests against zero.

## Native claims

| Claim | Evidence | How checked | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| The element frame inverse is `D3DXMatrixInverse( m, NULL, m )`, in place, with its return value ignored | v1.150 `CEFEffect_UpdateElementMatrices` 0xAF13D0 -> `D3DXMatrixInverse_Dispatch` 0x927518, then `D3DXMatrixMultiply_InPlace` | BN HLIL of AF13D0 | Confirmed |
| `D3DXMatrixInverse` returns NULL for a zero determinant before writing the output | Wine `dlls/d3dx9_36/math.c`; Microsoft's page says only that NULL is returned on failure | Read both | Confirmed (Wine source) |
| A zero rotation axis reaches a frame | `particle-rotation.ts` zero basis for `AxisVector4` length 0 (AFAB10) | Code read | Confirmed |

## Tests

- New in `tests/runtime/particle-graph.test.mjs`: a collapsed element frame (a zero-basis rotation on a kept-matrix element) and a collapsed holder frame both advance, with finite positions.
- Mutation: putting the throw back fails both tests (0 pass, 2 fail).
- Ran: all 76 `tests/runtime/particle-*.test.mjs` tests, `tsc --noEmit`, `pnpm --filter @sro/client-next verify:quick`, `pnpm task check:format`, `pnpm task check:source-encoding`. All exited 0.

Old-tab: safe - client-only arithmetic, no wire or asset change.

fix(nsgo): open DeviceHub or Simulator by bundle ID to show simulators

Fixes #826

## What

`bootSimulator` showed the simulator's window by running `open "$(xcode-select -p)/Applications/Simulator.app"` and ignoring the result. Xcode 27.2 no longer ships that app: DeviceHub.app (`com.apple.dt.Devices`, in `Xcode.app/Contents/Applications`) replaced it, so `nsgo run`, `nsgo dev` and `nsgo test` with an iOS, tvOS or watchOS simulator target never showed a window and said nothing.

Now `showSimulators` opens the app by bundle ID with `open -b`, trying DeviceHub first and Simulator (`com.apple.iphonesimulator`) for older Xcode, and `bootSimulator` prints a warning with both `open` errors when neither opens. Booting, installing and launching still go ahead without a window. `cmd/nsgo/ios.go` was the only place that opened the app (no other code or docs name `Simulator.app` or the bundle IDs).

## Tests

- `TestShowSimulators` covers the selection: DeviceHub installed (opens it, stops), only Simulator installed (falls back), neither (returns an error naming both).
- `TestBootSimulatorWaitsForReady` now stubs `open` instead of `xcode-select`, so it stays off the desktop, and checks the `open -b com.apple.dt.Devices` call.
- `go vet ./cmd/nsgo` and `go test ./cmd/nsgo` pass (Linux).

## Verification on Xcode 27.2

With DeviceHub not running, a test binary built from this branch that calls `bootSimulator` for a shut-down iPhone 18 Pro simulator (iOS 27.2) booted it, launched DeviceHub without a warning, and DeviceHub showed an on-screen window titled with the simulator's name. Before, the same path opened nothing.

## Screenshots

None (command-line tool change).

fix(controller): read the Application from the API server at each reconcile

## Context

When a replica of a new version restarts past its restart budget, the cluster controller stops that version. It pauses the Kubernetes Deployment and empties the new version's ReplicaSet, so the old version keeps serving. The stop is recorded in the Application's status, and every reconcile reads that status to decide whether the Deployment stays paused.

The controller read the Application from its local cache, and that cache can lag behind the status it just wrote. When a reconcile started right after the stop, its cached copy did not have the stop yet, so it applied the Deployment unpaused. Kubernetes then resumed the broken rollout until the next reconcile paused it again. That reconcile's status write failed on the stale copy, but the Deployment change had already gone through. `TestRestartBudgetStopsTheRevision` caught the Deployment in that unpaused window (#2775).

This PR makes each reconcile read the Application straight from the API server, so the objects it applies always follow the status the previous reconcile wrote.

## Changes

- `ApplicationReconciler.Reconcile` gets the Application through `APIReader` instead of the cache. That is one GET per reconcile, the same as the env secret read `ensureEnvSecret` already makes.

## Validation

- New envtest in `stop_envtest_test.go`. It stops a rollout, deletes the stopped revision's pod, then reconciles with a client whose cached Application predates the stop. The test checks that the Deployment stays paused and the stopped ReplicaSet stays at 0. Before the fix this case unpaused the Deployment.
- `go test ./...` in `controller` with envtest 1.37 passes, and `mise run lint:go` passes.
- The apps E2E shard runs `TestRestartBudgetStopsTheRevision` in CI.

Fixes #2775


## Minmax

| | Before | After | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| Production lines (+/-) | +2/-1 | +2/-1 | 0 |
| Test lines (+/-) | +57/-0 | +57/-0 | 0 |
| Files touched | 2 | 2 | 0 |

- Mechanisms/abstractions removed: none
- Not applied: none
- Verified: `go test ./...` in `controller` with envtest 1.37 passes; the new test fails with the fix reverted.
